newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's AMP says 96 new business strong.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's AMP says 96 new business strong.

text.p: Australia's largest life office, the Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Society said on Wednesday that new business was ahead of budget in recent weeks and was likely to continue.
AMP Chief General Manager Ray Greenshields also said it viewed the Australian sharemarket as being good value at the moment.
"New business has been very, very strong since early June. June, July and August have been superb and indications are that that's continuing," Greenshields told reporters.
"Our investment people see the Australian (share) market as being good value and we're heavily invested in the Australian market," he said.
He said there was some concern about the recent confrontation between the United States and Iraq, however he believed the situation would be resolved quickly.

"(The Gulf War) was very debilitating for the markets, so obviously what we hope is that it will be over and dealt with quickly and there's every reason to expect that that will be the case," he said.
Greenshields declined to comment on AMP's likely profit results in calendar 1996 as its performance largely depended on fluctuations in the investment markets.
"At this stage you need to look at what the markets have done," he said.
"However, we're happy with the way the year is unfolding."
